sentences: Grade inflation—the gradual increase in average GPAs (grade-point averages) over the past few decades—is often considered a product of a consumer era in higher education, in which students are treated like customers to be pleased.
But another, related force—a policy often buried deep in course catalogs called “grade forgiveness” —is helping raise GPAs.
translations: 分数膨胀——即过去几十年来平均绩点（GPA）的逐渐上升——通常被认为是高等教育消费时代的产物，在这个时代，学生被当作需要取悦的顾客。
但另一股相关的力量——一项通常深藏在课程目录中、名为“成绩宽恕”的政策——正在推高平均绩点。

sentences: Grade forgiveness allows students to retake a course in which they received a low grade, and the most recent grade or the highest grade is the only one that counts in calculating a student’s overall GPA.
translations: 成绩宽恕允许学生重修他们获得低分的课程，而在计算学生总平均绩点时，只有最近一次的成绩或最高分才算数。

sentences: The use of this little-known practice has accelerated in recent years, as colleges continue to do their utmost to keep students in school (and paying tuition) and improve their graduation rates.

When this practice first started decades ago, it was usually limited to freshmen, to give them a second chance to take a class in their first year if they struggled in their transition to college-level courses.
But now most colleges, save for many selective campuses, allow all undergraduates, and even graduate students, to get their low grades forgiven.
translations: 近年来，随着大学继续尽最大努力让学生留在学校（并支付学费）以及提高毕业率，这种鲜为人知的做法使用得越来越频繁。
几十年前这种做法刚开始时，通常仅限于大一新生，目的是如果他们在向大学课程过渡时遇到困难，给他们第二次机会重修第一年的课程。
但现在，除了许多精英型校园外，大多数大学允许所有本科生甚至研究生获得低分宽恕。

sentences: College officials tend to emphasize that the goal of grade forgiveness is less about the grade itself and more about encouraging students to retake courses critical to their degree program and graduation without incurring a big penalty.

“Ultimately,” said Jack Miner, Ohio State University’s registrar, “we see students achieve more success because they retake a course and do better in subsequent courses or master the content that allows them to graduate on time.”
translations: 大学官员往往强调，成绩宽恕的目标与其说是关于成绩本身，不如说是为了鼓励学生重修对其学位课程和毕业至关重要的课程，而无需承担重大惩罚。
“最终，”俄亥俄州立大学的教务长杰克·迈纳说，“我们看到学生取得更大的成功，因为他们重修了一门课程，并在后续课程中表现更好，或者掌握了让他们能按时毕业的内容。”

sentences: That said, there is a way in which grade forgiveness satisfies colleges’ own needs as well.

For public institutions, state funds are sometimes tied partly to their success on metrics such as graduation rates and student retention—so better grades can, by boosting figures like those, mean more money.

And anything that raises GPAs will likely make students—who, at the end of the day, are paying the bill—feel they’ve gotten a better value for their tuition dollars, which is another big concern for colleges.
translations: 话虽如此，成绩宽恕在某种程度上也满足了大学自身的需求。
对于公立院校来说，州政府资金有时部分与它们在毕业率和学生保留率等指标上的成功挂钩——因此，更好的成绩可以通过提高这些数字来意味着更多的资金。
而且，任何能提高平均绩点的措施都可能让学生——归根结底是他们在买单——觉得他们的学费花得更值，这是大学关心的另一个大问题。

sentences: Indeed, grade forgiveness is just another way that universities are responding to consumers’ expectations for higher education.
Since students and parents expect a college degree to lead to a job, it is in the best interest of a school to turn out graduates who are as qualified as possible—or at least appear to be.
On this, students’ and colleges’ incentives seem to be aligned.
translations: 事实上，成绩宽恕只是大学回应消费者对高等教育期望的另一种方式。
既然学生和家长期望大学学位能带来工作，那么学校培养出尽可能合格——或者至少看起来合格——的毕业生才最符合其自身利益。
在这一点上，学生和大学的动机似乎是一致的。

sentences:
26. What is commonly regarded as the cause of grade inflation?
A. Colleges’ neglect of GPAs.
B. The influence of consumer culture.
C. Students’ indifference to GPAs.
D. The change of course catalogs.
translations:
26. 通常被认为是什么导致了成绩膨胀？
A. 大学对GPA的忽视。
B. 消费文化的影响。
C. 学生对GPA的漠不关心。
D. 课程目录的变化。

sentences:
27. What was the original purpose of grade forgiveness?
A. To maintain colleges’ graduation rates.
B. To increase universities’ income from tuition.
C. To prepare graduates for a challenging future.
D. To help freshmen adapt to college learning.
translations:
27. 成绩宽恕的初衷是什么？
A. 为了维持大学的毕业率。
B. 为了增加大学来自学费的收入。
C. 为了让毕业生为充满挑战的未来做好准备。
D. 为了帮助新生适应大学学习。

sentences:
28. According to Paragraph 5, grade forgiveness enables colleges to
A. obtain more financial support.
B. improve their teaching quality.
C. boost their student enrollments.
D. meet local governments’ needs.
translations:
28. 根据第五段，成绩宽恕使得大学能够
A. 获得更多的财政支持。
B. 提高他们的教学质量。
C. 增加他们的学生招生人数。
D. 满足地方政府的需要。

sentences:
29. What does the phrase“to be aligned” (Para. 6) most probably mean?
A. To counterbalance each other.
B. To be contradictory to each other.
C. To be identical with each other.
D. To complement each other.
translations:
29. 短语“to be aligned”（第6段）最可能的意思是？
A. 相互抵消。
B. 相互矛盾。
C. 彼此相同。
D. 相互补充。

sentences:
30. The author examines the practice of grade forgiveness by
A. assessing its feasibility.
B. listing its long-run effects.
C. comparing different views on it.
D. analyzing the causes behind it.
translations:
30. 作者通过以下哪种方式审视了成绩宽恕的做法？
A. 评估其可行性。
B. 列举其长期影响。
C. 比较对其的不同观点。
D. 分析其背后的原因。
